title: A car losing value: an exponential model

stimulus.title: The value of a used car
stimulus.html:
A used car loses value over time. Its value is $24,000$24{,}000 one year after it was bought new and $14,500$14{,}500 four years after it was bought. The value of the car, in dollars, is modeled by the function CC given by C(t)=abtC(t) = ab^t, where tt is the number of years since the car was bought new.
Value of the car, in dollars, t years after it was bought new
tt (years)14
Value (dollars)24,00014,500

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Use the given data to write two equations that can be used to find the values of the constants aa and bb in the expression for C(t)C(t).

rubric.point: Both equations correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">ab = 24{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">ab^4 = 14{,}500</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: an equivalent pair, such as the ratio b^3 = 14500/24000 together with one of the equations

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Find the values of aa and bb as decimal approximations.

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>28389.581</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = 28389.581...</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.845</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = 0.845...</annotation></semantics></math> (both correct to three decimal places)
accept: values truncated to three decimal places

parts.sample: Dividing the equations: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>14</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>500</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b^3 = \frac{14{,}500}{24{,}000}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>14</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>500</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \left(\frac{14{,}500}{24{,}000}\right)^{1/3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0.845381</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0.845381...</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow><mi>b</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{24{,}000}{b}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>28389.581350</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 28389.581350...</annotation></semantics></math>. Both are stored in the calculator.

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of change of CC over the interval 1≤t≤41 \le t \le 4. Express your answer using correct units.

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3166.667</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3166.667</annotation></semantics></math> dollars per year, with the difference quotient and units
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>14500</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>24000</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{14500 - 24000}{4 - 1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3166.666</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -3166.666...</annotation></semantics></math> dollars per year

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3166.667</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3166.667</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3166.666</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3166.666</annotation></semantics></math> dollars per year

parts.sample: The average rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 4]</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{C(4) - C(1)}{4 - 1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>14</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>500</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{14{,}500 - 24{,}000}{3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3166.667</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -3166.667</annotation></semantics></math> dollars per year.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Use the average rate of change from part B(i) to estimate the value of the car at t=3t = 3 years. Show the work that leads to your answer.

rubric.point: An estimate of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>17666.667</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17666.667</annotation></semantics></math> dollars from a point on the secant line through <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 24{,}000)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>500</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4, 14{,}500)</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>24000</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3166.666</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24000 + (-3166.666...)(3 - 1)</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>14500</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3166.666</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14500 - (-3166.666...)(4 - 3)</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: The secant line through <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 24{,}000)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>500</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4, 14{,}500)</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3166.666</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 24{,}000 - 3166.666...(t - 1)</annotation></semantics></math>. At <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3166.666</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24{,}000 - 3166.666...(2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>17666.667</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 17666.667</annotation></semantics></math>. The estimate is about 17666.67 dollars.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Is the estimate in part B(ii) an overestimate or an underestimate of C(3)C(3)? Give a reason for your answer, using the concavity of the graph of CC on the interval 1≤t≤41 \le t \le 4.

accept: the estimate is greater than the model value C(3)

rubric.point: A reason from concavity on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 4]</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> is concave up there (decreasing, with its rate of change increasing), so the graph lies below the secant line
accept: "a > 0 and 0 < b < 1, so the graph of C is concave up on [1, 4]; the secant line lies above the graph, so the secant estimate is too large"
the average rates of change over equal intervals increase (become less negative), so C is concave up and the graph is below the secant line

parts.sample: Overestimate. On <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 4]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C(t) = ab^t</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a > 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>b</mi><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < b < 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing and concave up: the rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> is increasing. A concave-up graph lies below its secant line on the interval, so the point on the secant line at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math> is above the graph, and the estimate <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>17666.667</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17666.667</annotation></semantics></math> is greater than <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>17152.039</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C(3) = 17152.039</annotation></semantics></math>.
